ai.description: *Raorchestes leucolatus* is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brownish dorsum and distinct white patches on the groin. It features a pointed snout and granular skin. Family: Rhacophoridae. IUCN: DD.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes leucolatus* is best distinguished by the distinct, stark white patch on its groin and hidden surfaces of the thighs, which is absent in similar bush frogs.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes leucolatus* inhabits the evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found in high-altitude montane shola grasslands and forest edges above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The White Groin Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for small insects among the foliage of forest understories.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes leucolatus* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. Breeding occurs during the monsoon, with females laying small clutches of terrestrial eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes leucolatus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the high-elevation forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu above 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The call of *Raorchestes leucolatus* is a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude evergreen forests.
